temporal.dataset_source: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce public dataset (local raw CSVs); observational, not synthetic
temporal.outcome: among orders purchased in the next 90 days, any observed delivery >0 days later than estimate or review score <=2; outcomes are observed for up to 30 additional days
temporal.feature_cutoff: only orders delivered by cutoff; reviews are available only when review answer timestamp <= cutoff; missing review timestamps are treated as unavailable
temporal.scope: retrospective temporal observational benchmark; repeated seller snapshots may occur across periods; no causal or ROI claim
limitations: small local Olist extract, finite historical period, and sellers/orders are not independent
outcomes include only orders with delivery recorded by the end of the 30-day grace period; incomplete or undelivered orders do not contribute, which can bias observed risk
sellers with no delivered future order in the purchase window are omitted because their outcome is unknown
review answer timestamp is used to gate historical review features; missing timestamps are treated as unavailable
no calibration, decision threshold selection, prospective deployment, or intervention evaluation
features and labels summarize overlapping seller histories
cross-validation does not simulate prediction at a historical cutoff
survival concordance is apparent in-sample and is not a held-out estimate
no intervention experiment supports causal savings or ROI claims

interpretation: The published extract and complete release have different coverage and prevalence.

The original and fixed temporal code ran from the same verified full release and the same schedule. Their comparison isolates the combined availability and training-label changes, while evaluated cohorts can change.

The retrospective training code did not change. Its reported comparison uses the published extract and complete release, so it illustrates dataset and runtime differences rather than the temporal fix.
